_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The Germantown Power Plant burns natural gas or No.2 distillate fuel oil in five combustion turbine units to generate electricity for distribution during times of peak power demand. The station is subject to the Risk Management Plan (RMP) regulations because it has a turbine inlet air cooling system which contains anhydrous ammonia in excess of the threshold quantity listed in the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's RMP regulations. This system was originally installed in 2000 to increase electrical generating capacity in the summer months by cooling the turbine inlet air. The inlet cooling system was retired in 2009, but recommissioned in 2024-2025. The recommissioned system was charged with anhydrous ammonia in 2025.

Cooling the inlet air to a combustion turbine increases its power output. The anhydrous ammonia is used in a closed loop refrigeration system to make ice to keep the water in the storage tanks cold. The turbine inlet air is cooled by the cold water circulating inside cooling pipes at the turbine inlet. There are two identical, totally enclosed refrigeration systems designed to current International Institute of Ammonia Refrigeration (IIAR) Standards. 
A significant release of ammonia to the environment is highly unlikely. The Germantown Power Plant has completed a safety and design review under OSHA Process Safety Management Regulations, 2 CFR 1910.119. This requires a complete analysis of the anhydrous ammonia process from a catastrophic release and safety perspective prior to it being placed into service. It is We Energies policy to not only adhere to the Federal and State laws and regulations governing the use of this chemical, but to extend safety, health, and environmental efforts beyond government requirements. We Energies and its employees are committed to the safety and health of the employees and the welfare of our community. The Germantown Power Plant is supported by the internal corporate safety, health, and environmental staff as well

as a number of outside professional consultants. 

THE GENERAL ACCIDENTIAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLANNING: The Germantown Power Plant is a non-responding facility. The facility complies with the OSHA Process Safety Management Standard for anhydrous ammonia. As part of the requirements, a Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) was performed. As a result of this analysis, the process and instrument diagrams (P&ID's) were reviewed as part of the accident prevention program. Valves and headers have been placed on the roof where possible to reduce potential exposure of employees. This also reduces the potential of strike damage. Component parts are also being replaced based upon a specific schedule as established under mechanical integrity. The system is also being evaluated for leaks via system monitoring. All workers involved with the system have been trained regarding system safety and operation. All operations are supported by written operating instructions. An emergency response plan in the case of an ammonia release has been prepared. It has also been provided for review to both the Washington County LEPC and the Germantown Fire Department.  It is updated as needed by We Energies corporate safety, environmental, and health staff. Changes to improve safety are an on-going process within We Energies. All future changes in the ammonia system will follow the Management of Change component of the Process Safety Management Plan as prescribed by OSHA. 

FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY: No accidents involving the ammonia system have occurred since the system was placed into service in 2000, retired in 2009, and recommissioned in 2025.
